title: Remote access, batches 2 and 3 — what your phone will show

steps.path: Phone → any conversation, while the connection to your computer is down
steps.headline: While the phone reconnects, a grey line at the top says so and keeps your draft.
steps.changed: Today nothing on screen changes when the connection drops; the message box simply refuses to send. A grey line now sits above the messages: Reconnecting to your computer, your draft is kept.
steps.notice: It is its own row above the chat, not a banner over it, so no message is hidden. It disappears by itself when the connection is back.
steps.risk: Simulated: the workbench cannot drop a real connection, so the line is shown in place rather than triggered.

steps.path: Phone → any conversation, after a reconnect the computer could not fully answer
steps.headline: After a refresh that didn't finish, the phone admits it may be behind and offers Refresh.
steps.changed: Today a refresh that comes back incomplete changes nothing: the phone silently keeps what it had. The same line, in amber, now says the conversation may be behind your computer, why, and gives one button.
steps.notice: What you were reading stays put. Refresh asks the computer for a fresh copy; the line turns grey while it catches up and goes away when it is done.
steps.risk: The words are the longest on any phone screen in the app; the tester's shorter wording, if any, is applied before this reaches you.

steps.headline: Projects → Files works from the phone: the same list the desktop shows.
steps.changed: Today the computer refuses every file list from a phone. The refusal now lands as the same folder view the desktop has — folders, files, search, grid or list.
steps.notice: Same private paths stay hidden, same folders you saved. Only the width is different.
steps.risk: The Before picture shows the refusal the way this branch draws it (an error with Retry). The app you have today shows a spinner that never ends — one of two silent failures this batch fixes.

steps.path: Phone → menu → Session Files → a file
steps.headline: A file opens on the phone, and Download sits where Open and Reveal sit on the desktop.
steps.changed: Today the drawer says Nothing here yet and a file cannot open. Now the list fills, a file opens in the same viewer the desktop uses, and the toolbar shows a Download button in place of the two desktop-only ones.
steps.notice: Download saves the whole file to your phone's own downloads folder; a big one does not block the chat. Copy path, expand and close are where they were.
steps.risk: The Before picture shows the refusal as this branch draws it (could not load, with Retry). Today's app says Nothing here yet for a chat with thirteen files.

steps.headline: A file too big to preview shows its name, size and kind with Download, not a dead end.
steps.changed: A file over the phone's preview limit is not fetched at all. The computer answers with its size, and the phone shows a card: the name, 24.0 MB · PDF, one line saying why, and Download.
steps.measured: 24.0 MB PDF; previews stop at 1 MB for text and 10 MB for images and PDFs
steps.notice: Nothing freezes and nothing downloads until you ask. The desktop keeps its own, larger limits.
steps.risk: The limits are the ones you picked on the questions deck; changing them later is a one-line change, not a redesign.

steps.headline: Previews on the phone are sealed exactly as on the desktop, and downloads are always saved, never displayed.
steps.changed: Stated, not asked, after your question on the one-liner deck. The desktop already draws a web-page preview inside a box the browser walls off; the phone uses the same box, so a file cannot read the app around it. There is no second address. A file handed to the phone is marked save-this, so the browser never opens it as a page.
steps.notice: Nothing you can see differs between phone and desktop previews. The milestone's safety requirement is met without a second door, a second certificate, or a slower first preview.

steps.path: Phone → Projects → Files, and Session Files, when the computer cannot answer
steps.headline: Two silent failures become honest: the Files tab no longer spins forever, and the drawer no longer says Nothing here yet.
steps.changed: Stated, not asked. Found while drawing these screens: when the computer refuses or fails a file list, the Files tab showed Loading files… for ever, and the session drawer showed the empty-state message as if it knew. Both now show the real message with Retry.
steps.notice: You will only ever see these on a real failure; after batch 3 the phone is not refused any more. They also apply on the desktop, where a failed list used to look empty.
